newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PIPE MAKER HUTA FERRUM PRICES IPO AT PLN 11.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PIPE MAKER HUTA FERRUM PRICES IPO AT PLN 11.

text.p: Polish pipe maker Huta Ferrum SA, which seeks a main market listing on the Warsaw bourse, has set the price of its three-million-share initial public offering at 11 zlotys per share, the company said on Friday.
The firm's Friday statement did not say how many shares the issue's underwriters, HSBC Investment Bank plc and PBR, would underwrite. The standby fee is three percent.
Ferrum's financial adviser, HSBC Investment Services, had previously said the final price would be between 11 and 14 zlotys and that foreign investors would buy most of the shares.
The offering's 2.4-million-share large-investor tranche takes place on February 25 and 26 and the 600,000-share small investor tranche lasts from February 26 to March 3.
The firm has said it seeks its main market debut on May 19.

HSBC Investment Services said 350,000 shares in the large- investor tranche would be reserved for National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme, divided proportionally according to their current stakes in the firm.
NFI No.1 is Ferrum's largest shareholder, with a 33-percent stake, followed by the state treasury, with 25.1 percent and the firm's employees with 15 percent.

Ferrum made a net profit of 3.2 million zlotys in 1995 on 161.1 million zlotys in sales. It expects its net to fall to 2.9 million zlotys in 1996 before rebounding to 4.9 million zlotys in 1997. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
